officialTitle: Suppression of Ovarian Function Trial (SOFT) and Tamoxifen and Exemestane Trial (TEXT): adjuvant ovarian suppression with exemestane or tamoxifen in premenopausal breast cancer

design.sampleSizeSourceQuote: The primary analysis combined data from 4690 patients in the two trials.
primaryEndpoints: Joint TEXT+SOFT: DFS, exemestane+OFS vs tamoxifen+OFS
SOFT: DFS, tamoxifen+OFS vs tamoxifen alone
design.notes: Two companion phase 3 trials. SOFT randomised 3066 women to tamoxifen, tamoxifen + OFS or exemestane + OFS; TEXT randomised to tamoxifen + OFS or exemestane + OFS. OFS by triptorelin, oophorectomy or ovarian irradiation. This record holds the joint analysis and the SOFT-specific analyses as separately labelled outcomes.

clinicalQuestion: In premenopausal women with HR+ early breast cancer, does adding ovarian function suppression to tamoxifen, or using exemestane plus ovarian suppression, improve outcomes over tamoxifen-based therapy?

pico.population: Premenopausal women with hormone-receptor-positive early breast cancer
pico.intervention: Exemestane plus ovarian function suppression (TEXT/SOFT); tamoxifen plus ovarian function suppression (SOFT)
pico.comparator: Tamoxifen plus ovarian function suppression (joint analysis); tamoxifen alone (SOFT)
pico.outcomes: DFS, freedom from breast cancer, OS, adverse events

outcomes.sourceQuote: After a median follow-up of 68 months, disease-free survival at 5 years was 91.1% in the exemestane-ovarian suppression group and 87.3% in the tamoxifen-ovarian suppression group (hazard ratio for disease recurrence, second invasive cancer, or death, 0.72; 95% confidence interval [CI], 0.60 to 0.85; P<0.001).

The rate of freedom from breast cancer at 5 years was 92.8% in the exemestane-ovarian suppression group, as compared with 88.8% in the tamoxifen-ovarian suppression group (hazard ratio for recurrence, 0.66; 95% CI, 0.55 to 0.80; P<0.001).

With 194 deaths (4.1% of the patients), overall survival did not differ significantly between the two groups (hazard ratio for death in the exemestane-ovarian suppression group, 1.14; 95% CI, 0.86 to 1.51; P=0.37).

After a median follow-up of 67 months, the estimated disease-free survival rate at 5 years was 86.6% in the tamoxifen-ovarian suppression group and 84.7% in the tamoxifen group (hazard ratio for disease recurrence, second invasive cancer, or death, 0.83; 95% confidence interval [CI], 0.66 to 1.04; P=0.10).

Most recurrences occurred in patients who had received prior chemotherapy, among whom the rate of freedom from breast cancer at 5 years was 82.5% in the tamoxifen-ovarian suppression group and 78.0% in the tamoxifen group (hazard ratio for recurrence, 0.78; 95% CI, 0.60 to 1.02).

In SOFT, the 8-year disease-free survival rate was 78.9% with tamoxifen alone, 83.2% with tamoxifen plus ovarian suppression, and 85.9% with exemestane plus ovarian suppression (P=0.009 for tamoxifen alone vs. tamoxifen plus ovarian suppression).

The 8-year rate of overall survival was 91.5% with tamoxifen alone, 93.3% with tamoxifen plus ovarian suppression, and 92.1% with exemestane plus ovarian suppression (P=0.01 for tamoxifen alone vs. tamoxifen plus ovarian suppression)

DFS remained significantly improved with tamoxifen plus OFS versus tamoxifen (hazard ratio, 0.82; 95% CI, 0.69 to 0.98) with a 12-year DFS of 71.9% with tamoxifen, 76.1% with tamoxifen plus OFS, and 79.0% with exemestane plus OFS.

OS was improved with tamoxifen plus OFS versus tamoxifen (hazard ratio, 0.78; 95% CI, 0.60 to 1.01) and was 86.8% with tamoxifen, 89.0% with tamoxifen plus OFS, and 89.4% with exemestane plus OFS at 12 years.

safety.sourceQuote: Selected adverse events of grade 3 or 4 were reported for 30.6% of the patients in the exemestane-ovarian suppression group and 29.4% of those in the tamoxifen-ovarian suppression group

safety.description: Grade 3 or higher adverse events (8-year update; experimental = exemestane + OFS, control = tamoxifen alone; tamoxifen + OFS 31.0%)
safety.sourceQuote: Grade 3 or higher adverse events were reported in 24.6% of the tamoxifen-alone group, 31.0% of the tamoxifen-ovarian suppression group, and 32.3% of the exemestane-ovarian suppression group.

strengths: Two large companion randomised trials with long-term follow-up (up to 12 years in SOFT)
Stratification by prior chemotherapy allows risk-based interpretation
limitations: Primary SOFT comparison was not significant in the overall population at the first analysis
Higher adverse-event burden with ovarian suppression; adherence and quality-of-life considerations are relevant

clinicalImplications.text: Supports adding ovarian function suppression to adjuvant endocrine therapy for premenopausal women with HR+ breast cancer at sufficient risk to warrant chemotherapy, with exemestane plus ovarian suppression further reducing recurrence compared with tamoxifen plus ovarian suppression.

tumourBoardPearl.text: Benefit from ovarian suppression concentrates in higher-risk premenopausal women (e.g. those who received chemotherapy and remained premenopausal); for low-risk women tamoxifen alone remains reasonable.

curation.notes: Numbers transcribed from PubMed abstracts of PMIDs 24881463 (joint TEXT+SOFT), 25495490 (SOFT primary), 29863451 (8-year update) and 36493334 (SOFT 12-year). Drug slug 'triptorelin' reflects the GnRH agonist named in the joint-analysis abstract.
